title: Recipe Cards: tape diagrams and double number lines
goal: Students can show a ratio with a tape diagram, use equal parts to scale it, and read equivalent ratios on a double number line.

scenes.say: Welcome to the Recipe Cards station at the Pet Café. In this lesson you will use two pictures, tape diagrams and double number lines, to scale a recipe up.

show.sub: Tape diagrams and double number lines · Pet Café, station 2

scenes.say: Here is a recipe card. Puppy mix uses 3 scoops of kibble for every 2 treats. The ratio of kibble to treats is 3 to 2.

show.heading: A ratio compares two amounts
items: Puppy mix: 3 scoops of kibble for every 2 treats

scenes.say: A tape diagram shows the ratio as equal boxes. Kibble gets 3 boxes and treats get 2 boxes. Every box is the same size, so every box stands for the same amount.

show.heading: A tape diagram
show.caption: 3 boxes of kibble, 2 boxes of treats

say: Now a big order uses 15 scoops of kibble. How many treats go with it?
The kibble is 3 boxes, and those 3 boxes hold 15 scoops.
So one box is 15 divided by 3, which is 5.
Treats are 2 boxes, so the treats are 2 times 5, which is 10 treats.

show.heading: Scale it up with the tape
show.problem: The recipe uses 15 scoops of kibble. How many treats?

say: A double number line shows the same thing in a different way. The top line counts scoops of kibble, and the bottom line counts treats.
Every tick lines up a matching pair. 3 scoops go with 2 treats, 6 go with 4, 9 go with 6, and 15 scoops go with 10 treats. Each pair is an equivalent ratio.
The top and bottom numbers always grow by the same jumps. Kibble jumps by 3 and treats jump by 2.
Each pair of ticks is also a row in a ratio table, so you can move between the two pictures.

show.heading: Reading the double number line
items: Top jumps by 3, bottom jumps by 2: the same number of jumps
Each pair of ticks is one row of a ratio table

scenes.say: Your turn. A drink uses 4 cups of water for every 3 scoops of mix. How much water goes with 12 scoops? Pause the video and choose.
scenes.answer: The answer is 16 cups. 12 scoops is 4 groups of 3 scoops, so the water is 4 groups of 4 cups, which is 16 cups. Adding 9 to both amounts does not keep the ratio the same.

question.prompt: A drink uses 4 cups of water for every 3 scoops of mix. How many cups of water go with 12 scoops?

say: To sum up: a ratio compares two amounts.
In a tape diagram every box is the same size, so find what one box is worth, then scale.
On a double number line, matching ticks are equivalent ratios. Now head to the Recipe Cards station and practice!

show.heading: What to remember
items: Tape diagram: find one box, then scale
Double number line: matching ticks are equivalent ratios
